Hi Priyom / Neha,

Thanks for the SIG upload earlier. While reviewing your answers we flagged Q48 ("Describe maintenance windows and the types of events included") as ambiguous for our control review. Specifically: does your definition of "maintenance windows" include transient autoscaling eviction/instance restarts (e.g., short-lived preemptible evictions or orchestration-driven rescheduling), or only planned maintenance that may cause >5 minute downtime?

We need a written interpretation we can include in our risk assessment. Subject: Meeting notes: SIG Q48 — agreed interpretation

Notes from today's 30m call (joined: Elise, Rajesh; internal: Priyom, Neha, Marissa):

Summary outcome — written interpretation (agreed verbally):
- "Maintenance windows" for REDWOOD HOSTED inference are defined as scheduled, planned activities initiated by Redwood or a partner that may result in application-level downtime or degraded service lasting longer than 5 continuous minutes. Examples: kernel/hypervisor patches requiring node drain, planned OS-level patching causing pods to be cordoned, major orchestrator upgrades.
- Transient autoscaler events and preemptible instance evictions that cause short-lived reconvergence (typically < 60 seconds) are not considered "maintenance windows" for the purposes of SIG Q48; they are operational transient events.
- For autoscaler-driven rescheduling that results in > 5 minutes of customer-observable unavailability (rare), that event will be categorized as a maintenance window if pre-announced or part of a rolling maintenance plan.

Evidence we agreed to provide:
1) Runbook excerpt: "Maintenance vs transient events" (attached).
2) SOC2 Type II summary excerpt referencing change/maintenance controls (attached).
3) A short written statement (below) you can paste into the SIG response: see "Redwood written interpretation" message.

Open items:
- Elise requested a brief uptime histogram for autoscaler reconverges vs planned maintenance for last quarter; Priyom to follow up if FinBank needs the raw numbers (may take ~3 business days).

Thanks all — action: Priyom will circulate the written interpretation and attachments.

Elise / Rajesh —

Per our call last week, please find below the written interpretation you can place in your SIG response and the attachments referenced in the meeting notes. Let me know if you want any small edits to match FinBank's control language.

Redwood written interpretation (SIG Q48):
"Maintenance windows refer to scheduled, planned operational activities initiated by Redwood or its managed partners that are expected to cause customer-visible downtime or degraded service that persists for more than five (5) continuous minutes. Typical maintenance activities include planned OS/hypervisor patches requiring node drain, orchestrator upgrades with rolling restarts, and scheduled hardware maintenance. Short-lived autoscaler events — including preemptible instance evictions and transient pod rescheduling that result in reconvergence within approximately sixty (60) seconds — are considered transient operational events and are not classified as maintenance windows for the purposes of the SIG response. In the uncommon circumstance where an autoscaler-driven action results in customer-observable unavailability exceeding five (5) minutes and that action was scheduled or announced as part of a maintenance plan, it will be recorded and treated as a maintenance window."

Attached evidence:
- redwood_sig_q48_written_interpretation.pdf (this note as a PDF + sign-off)
- FinBank_SIG_Q48_context.png (screenshot of the SIG question with our answer highlighted)
- SOC2_Type2_summary_2026-09.pdf (section referencing change management and maintenance controls)

Optional: We can also provide the quarterly histogram of autoscaler reconverge durations (to show distribution of transient events vs planned maintenance). If you'd like that data, please confirm and we'll queue the telemetry request (ETA ~3 business days).

If this looks good, reply with "LGTM" and we'll mark Q48 as closed for evidence.
